content.title: Fil-Am Autumn Durald Arkapaw is the first woman to win a cinematography Oscar
content.text: Autumn Durald Arkapaw. Image: Instagram/@the__asc It was a heartfelt victory for Filipino-American Autumn Durald Arkapaw, who emerged as the first woman to win an Oscar for Best Cinematography at the 98th Academy Awards. Arkapaw brought home the coveted award at the 98th edition of the Oscars on Sunday, March 15 (morning of March 16 in the Philippines), for her work in Ryan Coogler’s “Sinners.” This is their second time working together in a film after “Black Panther: Wakanda Forever.” Even before her nomination at the ceremony, the cinematographer had been noted for being the first female to use Ultra Panavision and IMAX 65mm cameras in her shooting style. She is the only cinematographer to use an IMAX 15-perf camera with KODAK EKTACHROME film stock to date. Article continues after this advertisement Arkapaw’s win is also a win for female cinematographers, as the award has long been elusive to them. So far, she is the fourth female to be nominated for the category and the second Filipino to be recognized. In a March 2026 cover story for Vogue Philippines, she spoke about wanting to inspire other women to pick up a camera and discover the beauty of filmmaking, especially in telling stories that matter. “When you do these awards, you have to do a lot of talks and do these photoshoots, and even if that part of it feels uncomfortable to me, I’m okay with it, because I’m so proud of the film, and I want to show other girls that they can also be doing the same job,” she was quoted as saying. Arkapaw, who was born to a Filipino mom and Afro-Creole dad, also admitted that she hasn’t been able to visit the Philippines yet, but she’s “very in touch” with her Filipino heritage. “I’ve never been to the Philippines, but I’m very in touch with that side. And food was a big part of the culture,” she said. Arkapaw joins the growing list of Filipino-Americans making an impact in Hollywood. Robert Lopez is the first Filipino-American to win an Oscar for Best Original Song for “Frozen” through the hit “Let It Go,” in 2014, and “Remember Me” for “Coco” in 2018. /edv Your subscription could not be saved.
